words.m: a book that gives information for visitors about a place, such as a city or country
words.s: We bought a guidebook to learn about the best museums in Rome.

words.m: the metal bar with handles at the front of a bicycle or motorcycle that you use for steering
words.s: Hold the handlebars with both hands when you ride down the hill.

words.m: an area of water next to the coast, often protected by walls, where ships and boats can shelter
words.s: The fishing boats returned safely to the harbour before the storm.

words.m: a type of aircraft without wings that has large blades on top that go round
words.s: The rescue helicopter flew over the mountains to find the hikers.

words.m: to travel for free by standing by the road and asking drivers for a ride
words.s: It is not safe to hitchhike alone along a busy motorway at night.

words.m: the area at an airport or port where officials check the passports of people entering a country
words.s: We showed our passports at immigration after landing in London.

words.m: the act of travelling from one place to another, especially in a vehicle
words.s: The train journey from Galle to Colombo takes about two hours.

words.m: the bags, suitcases, and things that you take with you when you are travelling
words.s: You are allowed one piece of hand luggage on the aircraft.

words.m: a piece of equipment with moving parts that uses power to do a particular job
words.s: You can buy your train ticket from the machine at the station.

words.m: someone whose job is repairing the engines of vehicles and other machines
words.s: The mechanic repaired our car engine at the garage this morning.

words.m: the official right to belong to a particular country
words.s: Please write your full name and nationality on the arrival form.

words.m: travelling or staying somewhere as part of your work, not for a holiday
words.s: Her father has gone to Singapore on business for three days.

words.m: away from work or school for a holiday
words.s: The office is closed because the manager is away on vacation.

words.m: for or during the night
words.s: We took the overnight ferry and arrived early the next morning.

words.m: a person who is travelling in a vehicle but is not driving it or working on it
words.s: Every passenger must fasten their seatbelt before the plane takes off.

words.m: buses, trains, and other vehicles that anyone can pay to use
words.s: Using public transport helps to reduce traffic in the city centre.

words.m: the desk in a hotel or office building where visitors go when they first arrive
words.s: Please leave your room key at reception when you check out.

words.m: an arrangement in which something such as a seat or hotel room is kept for you
words.s: I called the hotel to make a room reservation for two nights.

words.m: a notice at the side of a road that gives information or instructions to drivers
words.s: The road sign warned drivers about a sharp bend ahead.

words.m: a sign by the side of a road or path that shows the direction and distance to places
words.s: We followed the wooden signpost pointing towards the village.

words.m: a vehicle that is able to travel in space
words.s: The astronauts travelled to the moon inside a silver spaceship.

words.m: a large flat box with a handle used for carrying clothes when you travel
words.s: She packed her warm winter clothes into a large blue suitcase.

words.m: an office that gives free maps, brochures, and advice to visitors
words.s: We got a free city map from the tourist information centre.

words.m: sets of red, amber, and green lights at road junctions that control traffic
words.s: Walk across the pedestrian crossing when the traffic lights turn green.

words.m: a long passage built underground or through a hill for a road or railway
words.s: The express train went through a long dark tunnel under the river.

words.m: a thick rubber ring that fits around the outside of a wheel on a car or bicycle
words.s: He had to stop by the road to change a flat tyre on his car.

words.m: a machine, usually with wheels and an engine, used for transporting people or goods
words.s: No motor vehicle is allowed to enter the pedestrian shopping street.

words.m: an official mark in your passport that allows you to enter or leave a country
words.s: You need to apply for a tourist visa before travelling to that country.

words.m: a room at a station, airport, or doctor's surgery where people can sit and wait
words.s: The passengers sat in the warm waiting room until the train arrived.

words.m: the large glass window at the front of a car, bus, or other vehicle
words.s: Clean the car windscreen carefully so you can see clearly in the rain.

features.gallery: Lazy gallery: no gallery DOM on boot; inactive cards use preload=none videos or lazy poster images. Bytes may load when Preview or Apply is used.

features.githubMedia: discoverGitHubMedia reads only the GitHub contents API for assets/ and normalises download_url, origin prefixes, /assets/, ?v= and #t= suffixes to ./assets/<file>
features.readability: #bgContrastScrim adaptive radial scrim, --bg-dim live slider (#sVideoDim) 0-75, 18% default, crisp 0 1px 2px text shadows in dark and light themes
features.photoWallpaper: #bgLivePhoto + #bgLivePhotoAmbilight with 12s auto-cycle for photos and ended-driven cycling for videos
features.crystalGlass: True backdrop-filter blur(14px) saturate(1.6) brightness(1.03), plus specular highlights.
features.playback: The video element avoids redundant reloads and has muted autoplay and stall recovery; playback still depends on browser policy, media availability and the device.
features.storage: v51 migrates earlier storage while preserving learner data and removes cleartext adminPin fields.
features.highlightedUi: High-contrast gradient primary actions and layered glass controls, cards and navigation.
features.rainbowLiquidGlass: v37: fully retired - no rainbow stripes, no neon glows, no glowing text shadows
features.springPhysics: v37: GPU-composited transform/opacity spring curves drive press, dock glide and screen/sheet morphs at 60-120fps
features.lowEnd: v37: single hardware video overlay, sleeping canvas, contain:layout style and transform-only transitions keep low-end phones smooth
features.instantResponse: v37: 0.04s press recognition, 0.16s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) spring release, 0.22s screen and sheet glide, GPU transform/opacity only, a 60ms debounced DB.save() and a canvas that ignores UI taps
features.typography: v37: Inter + Apple system stack for English, Noto Sans Sinhala / Sinhala Sangam MN / Nirmala UI for Sinhala at line-height 1.72, loaded from a runtime style tag (never a static <link>)
features.creditSpotlight: The intro plays once; one eight-second spotlight cycle follows. Dialogs appear above the credit.
features.englishDefault: English (lang "en", guideLang "en") remains the default, with an optional Sinhala switch inside the User Guide.
features.humanVoice: Single English words request a UK dictionary recording; the provider or device fallback determines the actual voice.
features.sessionFlow: Ready instruction, visual and spoken countdown, number + word, 650ms pause, same word again, five-second writing timer.
features.cleanWords: Single-word URLs contain the clean word without appended punctuation; multiword text is passed directly.
features.repeatReplay: Repeat announces the number and plays the same word twice. Slower uses playbackRate and defaultPlaybackRate 0.72.
features.noDeviceVoice: A device voice is used as a safety net when remote audio is unavailable.
features.voiceLifecycle: Starting, pausing, replaying, navigating or leaving cancels the audio element, the synth utterance and every timer.
features.testSound: Sound check streams the real Youdao studio audio without a debug pill.
features.numberedWords: Number N, a 180ms pause, the word, a 650ms pause, then the same word again.
features.pauseResume: Pause cancels the current timers and audio; resume waits for its spoken prompt before restarting the current word.
features.finishSummary: The spoken completion summary is also rendered in the results screen.
features.tts: One Youdao en-GB stream with pinned British device voice fallback if media fails.
features.voice: British dictionary audio with preferred British female device voice fallback.
features.fallback: Playback errors or a 2800ms start timeout fall back to a pinned device voice; availability varies.
features.dictationNumber: One Dictation #N progress label plus progress dots; duplicate word-card badges are removed.
features.bundledAudio: Removed: no generated or bundled MP3 pack; no synthetic formant, waveform or espeak audio.
features.countdown: Three, two, one on clock-anchored 1000ms beats; the first word starts at 3000ms.
features.voiceFallback: The same pinned British device voice is used for fallback where available.
features.guideAudio: Sinhala uses a sentence-chunked Sinhala stream or si-LK synthesis; no English romanisation.
features.helpers: Repeat, Slower, Repeat sentence and British letter names work during speaking and the writing window; the full five-second timer restarts.
features.session8: Session 8 - Personal Feelings, Opinions & Experiences (Adj), 29/10/2026, 30 adjectives with UK IPA, Sinhala meaning and example sentence
features.dataSheet: Interactive bilingual data report at /data and /data.html with a calculator and 30 playable rows. Byte figures are illustrative; actual browser and network usage varies.
features.zeroWaste: A four-element prebuffer prepares countdown cues and a rolling word window; actual network costs vary.
features.spelling: favourite/favorite and tyre/tire are both accepted
features.sinhalaGuideVoice: Sinhala stream or si-LK speechSynthesis; if unavailable the written guide remains accessible.
features.creditLock: v53: student playback only replays clips saved in data/elevenlabs-audio.json, IndexedDB or Cloud. api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech is called ONLY from the admin Generate button (ElevenVault.adminGenerateMissing) and never regenerates an existing clip.
features.crossDevice: v54: saving the API key, voice settings, wallpaper, session or words in Lecturer Mode on one PC appears on every other phone, tablet and laptop within a second.
features.studio: v53: the admin panel is a 3-step studio (word list + auto-complete + publish, permanent voice vault, one-time keys) with all legacy tools inside a collapsed Advanced section.
features.encryptedVault: v54: the ElevenLabs API key, the GitHub token, the voice settings, the session and the word list are encrypted as SDP_ENC_V1 URL-safe Base64 ciphertext keyed by the lecturer PIN (78987898 + salt). No raw API key or GitHub token is ever committed, so GitHub secret scanning stays quiet.
features.universalSync: v54: every lecturer save stamps syncRev, encrypts the vault and pushes three channels in parallel - the ntfy.sh zero-config relay (dictationb1_sdp_vault_v54), the Google Apps Script Cloud backend and a permanent GitHub commit of data/config.json, data/session.json, data/version.json and data/elevenlabs-audio.json.
features.audioRelay: v54: generated ElevenLabs clips are also published to the shared clip relay (dictationb1_sdp_audio_v54), so a phone without a GitHub token still receives the exact saved clips.
features.syncPull: v54: UniversalSync.pullAll() runs on boot, on visibilitychange, when Lecturer Mode unlocks and from the Sync Now button, cache-busting every JSON read and applying the highest syncRev.
